title: Variant interop snapshot for routing fallback resilience
creator: Maya Chen
description: Maintain a concise, machine-readable snapshot of variant interoperability relevant to the Smart Routing stack so that routing policies (region selection, tier routing, fallback selection) can make safe, low-latency decisions. This ticket produces a curated compatibility snapshot that captures tokenizer parity, context/window behaviours, and tooling constraints for all active model variants used in host/dedicated/private deployments. The snapshot will be consumed by: 1) routing decision service (region/tier/fallback selectors), 2) canary/rollout orchestration, and 3) ops runbooks for incident mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single JSON/CSV snapshot published to S3 and referenced by routing-service config; 2) Snapshot includes fields: model_variant, tokenizer_family, tokenization_diff_score, max_context_tokens, recommended_kv_cache_strategy, known_tooling_gaps; 3) CI checks that validate tokenization parity using canonical prompt set (bench-tokenize-v2) pass or register a tolerated-diff with mitigation; 4) Routing unit tests exercise at least three fallback scenarios (cross-region, tier-eviction, and busy-pool fallback) using the snapshot; 5) Runbook updated with clear operator steps when a variant is marked incompatible.
implementation_notes: Plan: - Stage 1: Create snapshot schema and generator job (Python) that pulls canonical metadata from model-catalog and tokenizer-tests. - Stage 2: Integrate snapshot publishing to s3://redwood-inference/compat-snapshots/{date}.json and add pointer to routing-service config. - Stage 3: Add CI job tokenize-parity-check that runs bench-tokenize-v2 against primary+fallback pairs and computes tokenization_diff_score; threshold configurable via environment. - Stage 4: Add opt-in feature flag to routing-service to enable snapshot-driven fallback gating; default remains permissive for canaries. - Utilities: small shim in routing-service to translate tokenizer_family -> token_mapper for legacy variants. See design notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SMART-ROUTING-COMPAT-SNAPSHOT
test_plan: - Unit tests for snapshot generator with mocked model-catalog. - End-to-end staging test: simulate routing-service calling snapshot for three scenarios: region outage, dedicated tier saturation, and model variant deprecation; assert fallback chosen has tokenization_diff_score <= configured threshold or alternative mitigation applied. - Performance: snapshot load latency must be <50ms on cold start; use caching TTL=5m. - Telemetry: emit compatibility_query and fallback_decision metrics to Grafana dashboard 'routing/compatibility'.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge generator and CI checks behind feature flag. 2) Publish initial snapshot for a 2-week observation window pointed at staging routing-service. 3) Enable feature flag in canary region (us-west-2) for tier-routing traffic <10%. 4) Monitor 'fallback-mismatch' alerts for 72 hours. 5) Gradually increase to 100% once no regressions are observed.
risks: - False negatives: overly strict tokenization_diff_score could force more expensive model fallbacks and increase latency. - False positives: overly lenient thresholds could allow incompatible variants to be selected, causing hallucinations or truncation. - Data drift: new model uploads can invalidate the snapshot quickly; need cadence for regeneration. - Tooling divergence: third-party tooling (quantization toolchains) may be incompatible even if tokenizer parity holds.
